title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a fragment, 'Ex. 2', from a list of examples of some abstract structure. Ex. 1 is not shown. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: Bourbaki-style drafts on Cauchy's theorem in several variables, so they give no context.

Setting, as best I can reconstruct it:
- A is a base ring (or scheme). O is presumably a finite locally free A-algebra.
- ℙ = ℙ(O/A) is a Picard-type (symmetric monoidal, invertible-object) category attached to O/A. The plausible reading is the category of invertible O-modules (or O-torsors) P.
- That category is equipped with the norm functor Nr_{O/A}: ℙ(O/A) → Pic(A). This is the classical norm of invertible modules or torsors.
- C is a category on which ℙ acts, (P, X) ↦ P ⊗_O X.

Definition. A 'norm' from C to ℙ (better: a ℙ-norm on C) is a pair (ν, α):
- ν: C → D is a functor to an A-linear category D on which Pic(A) acts. Grothendieck stresses that D is not fixed in advance.
- α_{X,P}: ν(P ⊗_O X) ≅ Nr_{O/A}(P) ⊗_A ν(X) is a system of isomorphisms, subject to transitivity (associativity with respect to P ⊗ P') and functoriality in P and X.

In modern terms, ν is a functor that is equivariant along the monoidal functor Nr: Pic(O) → Pic(A). It is a 'twisted-equivariant' or multiplicative-transfer functor.

Claim 1. Fix X in Ob C, implicitly assuming C is generated by X under the ℙ-action, i.e. C is a ℙ-torsor category. Then the category of norms with values in D is canonically equivalent to the category of objects T of D, via ν(P ⊗_O X) ≅ Nr(P) ⊗ T. This is the usual statement that equivariant functors out of a trivial torsor are determined by the image of a base point.

Claim 2. Suppose given a functorial trivialization Nr_{O/A}(P) ≅ A for P ∈ ℙ(O/A), compatible with the transitivity data. For instance, ℙ might be restricted to objects of trivial norm. Then the object ν(X) no longer depends on X up to canonical isomorphism.

Base-change setting:
- Let A' → A be a base change as in Ex. 1. Let C', D' be 'catégories de [?]' over A'.
- Let (ν, α): C' → D' be a norm, and φ: C → C' an admissible functor.
- Then there is a canonical object T_φ of D' together with isomorphisms ν(φ(X)) ≅ T_φ.
- So the composite C → C' → D' yields an invariant T_φ attached to φ, independent of X.

Marginal programme:
1. Generalize to the case where ℙ is replaced by any A-Picard-type category for which Nr_{O/A}(P) ⊗_A Y exists.
2. Show there is a universal D receiving a norm. This is a category V_A(C), the 'norm' or multiplicative pushforward of the category C.
3. V_A(C) commutes with base change as in Ex. 1.
4. Under the trivialization hypothesis, V_A(C) carries a canonical section T.

Purpose. Within 'Théorie de Galois des motifs', this looks like machinery for norms or Weil restriction at the level of categories (stacks, gerbes, fibred categories) along a finite extension. That is what one needs, for instance, to define multiplicative transfers or Weil-restricted Tannakian or motivic data, or canonical invariant objects such as determinants and discriminants attached to admissible functors.
errors: Claim 1 is only correct if C is generated by X under the ℙ-action (C a ℙ-torsor, or at least the orbit of X), with Aut(X) compatible with the action. As written, 'X fixé dans Ob C' leaves this hypothesis implicit.

Claim 2 also needs the action of automorphisms of P on Nr(P) ≅ A to be trivial, i.e. compatibility with the trivialization as automorphisms. Otherwise T_φ is canonical only up to a group of automorphisms. The note 'conditions de transitivité compatibles' gestures at this but does not spell it out.

The page is fragmentary. 'Ex. 1', the precise meaning of the category name (read 'Dennis'), 'admissible functor' and the base-change setup are not defined here, so the statements cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: Norm functor Nr_{O/A} on invertible modules or torsors for a finite locally free extension, used as a symmetric monoidal functor Pic(O) → Pic(A).
ideas.modern_name: Norm of line bundles or torsors (norm functor of Picard categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (EGA II 6.5 norm of invertible sheaves); Deligne, SGA4 XVII 6.3 (trace/norm of torsors)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §6.5 (norm of invertible modules); SGA 4 XVII (Deligne) for torsors

ideas.what: Functors ν: C → D with coherent isomorphisms ν(P⊗X) ≅ Nr(P)⊗ν(X), i.e. functors that are equivariant along the norm. Called 'normes' of a category.
ideas.modern_name: Norm (multiplicative transfer) functors on categories; cf. Ferrand's 'foncteur norme' on modules, and norms of categories/stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Ferrand, 'Un foncteur norme' (Bull. SMF 1998); later Bachmann–Hoyois norms in motivic homotopy (2017); tensor induction in Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel

ideas.what: A universal target V_A(C) receiving a norm from C, compatible with base change and carrying a canonical section under a trivialization of norms.
ideas.modern_name: Norm or multiplicative Weil restriction of a (linear or fibred) category: the universal multiplicative pushforward
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; related to Ferrand (norm of modules/algebras), Weil restriction of stacks, and Bachmann–Hoyois norm functors

ideas.what: Equivariant functors out of a torsor category correspond to objects of the target (ν determined by T = ν(X)).
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant functors from a trivial torsor are determined by their value on a base point

missed.claim: A programme to construct, for a finite extension O/A, a universal category V_A(C) receiving a 'norm' from an O-category C, i.e. one twisted-equivariant for Nr_{O/A}. The programme also asks that V_A(C) commute with base change and acquire a canonical section when norms are trivialized. The aim appears to be producing canonical invariant objects T_φ attached to admissible functors in a motivic/Galois context.
missed.quote: Montrer qu'il y a une D universelle recevant une fonction norme, d'où ... V_A(C) ... Noter que V_A(C) commute aux chgt de base
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates categorical norm/multiplicative-transfer constructions, e.g. Ferrand's norm functor (1998) and Bachmann–Hoyois norms on motivic categories (2017), here placed explicitly within Grothendieck's 1960s Galois theory of motives. It may be an early unrecorded instance of 'norms of categories' in a motivic setting. Its precise content is too fragmentary to claim a finished result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches a definition and a universal construction of norm functors at the level of categories, twisted-equivariant along Nr: Pic(O) → Pic(A), inside the motivic Galois notes. The idea is recognisable from later work (Deligne on torsor norms, Ferrand 1998, Bachmann–Hoyois). An early Grothendieck version of categorical norms is mildly notable, but the page is a fragmentary sketch with key terms undefined.
transcription_corrections: The category name read as 'Dennis' ('Dening ulli' in the hand) is uncertain. Possibly a named category type ('catégorie de Picard'? 'de Deligne'?); I cannot confirm from the image.
'Une norme de C à ℙ est un couple (ν, α)': the underlined phrase in the image looks like 'Une notion norme' or 'Une norme'. Read with caution.
Left margin, last note: 'Noter que V_A(C) commute aux chgt de base comme dans Ex. 1' seems to be preceded by a crossed-out 'Nr'/'K' expression.
Right margin: 'Noter qu'alors la catégorie V_A(C) est munie d'une section canonique T et V_C ... de base dans ...'. It is partly illegible and seems to continue onto the 'chgt de base' line.
The page number in the lower-left corner is 31 (archive numbering). The neighbouring pages (44, 46 of an analysis manuscript on Cauchy's theorem) are unrelated to this page.
